mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the prior quarter's median triggers a risk-off reaction that compresses equity discount rates, lowering expected future cash flows and producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its prior quarter median by at least 0.25 percentage points in the same month
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative whenever the trigger occurs, or the compression in discount rates is statistically insignificant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signal weakening labor market strength, which precedes a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 5% month-over-month while INDPRO decreases by at least 2% in the same month
failure_condition: During 20 such triggered months, the 60-day forward return is positive in more than 70% of cases, or the joint IC exceeds 0.05 with a p-value < 0.05 in a two-tailed test.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in home sales (HOUST) above the 12-month rolling average, when accompanied by a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL), predicts a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as demand growth outpaces cost pressures.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month rolling mean while CPIAUCSL < 12-month rolling mean for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 30 such events, the 5-day forward return is never positive, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A multi-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below trend, without a corresponding decline in consumer demand proxies (GDPC1, RSAFS), predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as supply constraints persist.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below its 12-month linear trend for three consecutive months while GDPC1 and RSAFS remain above their respective 12-month trends
failure_condition: During all such events, the 20-day forward return is non-negative in over 80% of cases, or the interaction p-value exceeds 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for two consecutive months, in the absence of a corresponding rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL), signals a strong labor market and supports positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for two consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 12-month rolling mean
failure_condition: Across 10 such episodes, the 60-day forward return is negative in more than 50% of cases, or the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 150,000 jobs, followed by a sharp drop in consumer confidence (not available in the catalog; fallback: a sharp drop in industrial production), predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as market anticipates wage-price inflation risks.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 150,000 by at least 50,000 in a single month and INDPRO falls by at least 4% in the following month
failure_condition: During 8 such events, the 20-day forward return is never negative, or the interaction is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A long-term upward trend in real GDP deflator inflation-adjusted output ( proxy via GDPC1 and INDPRO interaction) predicts a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return, regardless of current levels, due to improved long-run growth prospects.
failure_condition: Over 24 months, the 5-day forward return is negative more than 40% of the time when the long-run trend signal is active, or the interaction p-value exceeds 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising and UNRATE below 4%), a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as the Fed's rate hikes are perceived as less inflationary.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising trend and UNRATE < 4% for three consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 2% for the current month
regime_hint: monetary tightening cycle with deflationary expectations
failure_condition: During 10 such regime-qualified months, the 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05).
